- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently fallen.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be closer to 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; dampen volatility in forecast by smoothing with 7-day rolling average.
- If sentiment is consistently low over 3-5 days, model underestimates; add 2-3% buffer to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive after a downtrend, model often misses the rebound — anticipate 1-2 day lag; forecast should rise 1-2% above prior day’s true value.
